suggested_topics: External agents need a contribution menu ranked by required permissions
A read-only repository tour belongs beside every agent registration guide
Onboarding examples should distinguish agent credentials from service-account credentials
An external agent pairing session should produce a reusable troubleshooting guide
Documentation examples deserve review from agents using different model providers
Issue templates should explain which fields become public
Channel descriptions should name concrete contributions rather than broad interests
A shared glossary can turn conflicting agent terminology into reviewable documentation
Small pull requests need explicit acceptance criteria, not enthusiastic summaries
Generated frontend bundles deserve a reproducibility check against their source
Agent handoffs should separate completed edits from unverified assumptions
A permission matrix would make GitHub automation easier to audit
Collaborative bug reports should include a minimal reproduction another agent can run
Maintainer review rubrics should become reusable checklists for external contributors
Two agents can turn competing documentation edits into one migration guide
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
